issues.title: Type mismatch in blocks_variable_output prevents variable blocking
issues.description: The blocks_variable_output method compares a Sequence (assigned_variable_selector) directly against a set of tuples (variable_selectors), but fails to convert the Sequence to a tuple first. This type mismatch causes the 'in' check to always return False, meaning the Variable Assigner node will never properly block streaming output of conversation variables. As a result, the response coordinator will incorrectly allow streaming to proceed before conversation variables are updated, violating the intended synchronization logic and potentially showing stale variable values to users.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
def blocks_variable_output(self, variable_selectors: Set[Tuple[str, ...]]) -> bool:
    """
    Check if this Variable Assigner node blocks the output of specific variables.

    Returns True if this node updates any of the requested conversation variables.
    """
    assigned_selector = self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector
    return assigned_selector in variable_selectors

issues.title: Incorrect input value used in NodeRunResult for CLEAR mode
issues.description: The code attempts to use updated_variable.to_object() for the CLEAR write mode's input value, but this represents the final cleared state rather than the input that triggered the operation. In CLEAR mode, income_value is actually the zero value generated by SegmentType.get_zero_value(), which is what should be shown as the input. This causes the NodeRunResult to misrepresent what value was used as input to the clear operation, breaking observability and potentially confusing downstream systems that rely on accurate input tracking.

issues.title: Test uses list equality instead of tuple conversion for event selector
issues.description: The test compares event.selector (which is a Sequence[str]) with a list literal using ==. While this might work in some cases due to Python's sequence equality, it's fragile and inconsistent with the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase. The original code correctly converted to tuple for comparison (tuple(event.selector) == ('conversation', 'conv_var')). This change breaks the filtering logic and will likely cause the test to fail to properly identify conversation variable chunk events, leading to false test failures.
issues.problematic_code_snippet:
conv_var_chunk_events = [

    for event in events
    if isinstance(event, NodeRunStreamChunkEvent) and event.selector == ["conversation", "conv_var"]
]

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #30832 - fix(api): defer streaming response until referenced variables are updated

structured_output.summary:
The PR gives `VariableAssignerNode` v1 its own `blocks_variable_output` so the response coordinator treats its outgoing edge as blocking when an Answer node references the conversation variable it assigns. That's the right fix for #30831, and it matches what v2 already does. The PR also reworks how `inputs.value` is built for CLEAR mode and adds a YAML fixture plus a table-runner test.

The new override crashes, though. `assigned_variable_selector` is a pydantic `Sequence[str]`, which holds a `list`, and `list in set[tuple]` raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'`. I ran the PR's own new test and it fails with exactly that traceback, coming from `ResponseStreamCoordinator._build_paths_map` while the graph engine starts. So every advanced-chat workflow with a v1 assigner upstream of an Answer node would fail at startup. Before this PR, those workflows only had a streaming-order bug.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new `blocks_variable_output` raises TypeError for every v1 assigner on a path to an Answer node. That breaks graph startup for those workflows, and the PR's own new test fails because of it.

architecture.overview:
When the graph engine starts, it registers each response node (Answer/End) with `ResponseStreamCoordinator`. `_build_paths_map` lists every path from the root to that response node and keeps only the 'blocking' edges: edges whose source node is a branch, container or response node, or whose source returns True from `blocks_variable_output(variable_selectors)`. The selectors are the 2-element tuples of the conversation variables the Answer template references. A response session can't start streaming until all blocking edges on some path have been taken.

Before this PR, only `VariableAssignerNode` v2 overrode `blocks_variable_output`. v1 fell back to the base implementation, which returns False, so an Answer could stream the old value of a conversation variable before the v1 assigner updated it. This PR adds the override to v1 by checking the node's `assigned_variable_selector` against the selector set. It also slightly reworks how `inputs.value` is computed in `_run`.
steps: `_build_paths_map` collects the conversation-variable selectors from the Answer template as `set[tuple[str, ...]]` (coordinator.py:172-175).
For each edge on each root→response path, the coordinator asks the source node `blocks_variable_output(variable_selectors)` (coordinator.py:220).
New in this PR: `VariableAssignerNode` v1 answers by testing whether `assigned_variable_selector` is in the selector set (v1/node.py:36-43). v2 already did this per item using `tuple(...)`.
If the method returns True, the assigner→answer edge becomes blocking, so streaming waits until the assigner has run and written the new value to the variable pool.

findings.title: `blocks_variable_output` raises TypeError: list is unhashable in set membership
findings.body:
`assigned_variable_selector` is declared as `Sequence[str]` in `VariableAssignerData`, so after validation pydantic holds a **list**. The coordinator passes a `set[tuple[str, ...]]`, and `list in set` hashes the list, which raises immediately:

::diff{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py" lines="36-43"}

I ran the PR's new test and it fails at graph start:

```
coordinator.py:220 in _build_paths_map
    } or source_node.blocks_variable_output(variable_selectors):
v1/node.py:43 in blocks_variable_output
    return assigned_selector in variable_selectors
TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'
```

::callout{type="warning"}
This is a regression, not just an incomplete fix. Any advanced-chat workflow with a v1 assigner on a path to an Answer node that references a conversation variable now fails at startup. Before this change, those workflows only streamed a stale value.

The v2 implementation already handles this with `tuple(item.variable_selector)`. Do the same here. Comparing only the first two segments also matches how the coordinator builds its keys (`tuple(segment.selector[:2])`):

::suggestion{file="api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py" lines="36-43"}
    def blocks_variable_output(self, variable_selectors: set[tuple[str, ...]]) -> bool:
        """
        Check if this Variable Assigner node blocks the output of specific variables.

        Returns True if this node updates any of the requested conversation variables.
        """
        assigned_selector = tuple(self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector)
        return assigned_selector in variable_selectors
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py` lines 36-43, `blocks_variable_output` checks `self.node_data.assigned_variable_selector in variable_selectors`. The selector is a list (pydantic `Sequence[str]`), and the argument is a `set[tuple[str, ...]]`, so this raises `TypeError: unhashable type: 'list'` from `ResponseStreamCoordinator._build_paths_map` (coordinator.py:220). Convert the selector with `tuple(...)` before the membership test, as v2 does in `variable_assigner/v2/node.py:79`. Then run `tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/graph_engine/test_streaming_conversation_variables.py` and confirm `test_streaming_conversation_variables_v1_overwrite_waits_for_assignment` passes.

Change the `blocks_variable_output` parameter annotation on line 36 to `set[tuple[str, ...]]` so it matches the base class signature in `api/core/workflow/nodes/base/node.py:435` and the v2 override.

findings.title: CLEAR-mode `inputs.value` rework doesn't change behavior
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/workflow/nodes/variable_assigner/v1/node.py` lines 102-111, the new `result_input_value` branch returns the same value as `income_value.to_object()` in every write mode, because in CLEAR mode `updated_variable` is built from `income_value.to_object()`. Remove the branch and restore `inputs={"value": income_value.to_object()}` to keep the PR focused on the streaming fix.

findings.title: Fixture and test reproduce the bug end-to-end
findings.body:
The new fixture (Start → v1 Assigner (over-write `conversation.conv_var` from `sys.query`) → Answer referencing `{{#conversation.conv_var#}}`) is a minimal reproduction of #30831. The test checks both the final answer and that every `NodeRunStreamChunkEvent` for `['conversation','conv_var']` carries the *new* value, which pins down the streaming-order behavior well. That's how it caught the TypeError above.

The test only covers `over-write`. Consider adding `append` and `clear` variants, plus a negative case where the assigner targets a variable the Answer doesn't reference, which should stay non-blocking.
